inputs.original_text: Her 2026 State of the State agenda would make gunmakers share responsibility for weapons sold in New York being converted into illegal machine guns—and adds criminal penalties without saying who would face them. Preventing violence is a serious concern, but vague penalties and shifting responsibility onto an entire industry are no substitute for holding those who break the law accountable. The public deserves to know whether this is really aimed at manufacturers or whether the burden could spread to people who obey the law.
inputs.modified_text: This is another case of government reaching for an easy target instead of confronting people who turn guns into illegal machine guns. Her 2026 State of the State agenda would make gunmakers share responsibility for weapons sold in New York, while adding criminal penalties without even saying who would face them. That kind of vagueness invites officials to widen the burden from manufacturers to people who obey the law. Public safety matters, but punishing an entire industry won’t restore order or hold the actual lawbreakers accountable.
